title: A chg landing on an independent path is held until it is independently verified

story.i_want_to: a change chg landed that touches an independent path to be held until a separated verifier on another host has verified it
story.so_that: a self-modifying change that reaches master through chg gets the same independent verification Gate B gives a pull-request merge (US-52.12)

rationale: US-52.12 makes Gate B clear an independent path only when MergePrecondition.independent_verification/2 is :ok, but that gate runs before loopctl merges a pull request; on the chg route chg lands the change and loopctl is told afterwards, through the landed event. US-52.12 left that route to this story because the hold must leave over US-52.31's holder resolve edge, not a human one (nothing waits for Mark, PRD R4). Split from US-52.31 so a defect in the chg landing path never blocks the holder-resolve change the rest of release 5 depends on.

acceptance_criteria.description: Applying a chg landed event of a story whose repo has independent_paths enqueues, inside the event's own transaction, one Loopctl.Workers.ChgIndependentPathsWorker job whose args carry the landed revision (event.sha, the revision commit) and the merge_sha (data.merge_sha, the trunk commit), unique per (story_id, landed revision), and changes nothing else: the landing is recorded, the item is merged, and a missing chg review escalates it over :review_missing exactly as today, and a redelivered landed event enqueues no second job.

The job reads the diff that landed on trunk (PullRequestSource.compare/3 of merge_sha's first parent against merge_sha) and judges MergePrecondition.independent_verification/2 (US-52.12) for the landed revision, never for merge_sha. A compare that fails returns {:error, _} so Oban retries it (max_attempts 5, the worker's backoff); only the last attempt's failure counts as an unreadable diff. When the diff touches an independent path and the fact is not :ok, or the diff is unreadable, the job writes, under the story lock, an independent_hold stage event naming the landed revision, whatever the item's stage, and then: at merged or deployed it escalates the item over the new control-only edge {from, :escalated, :independent_unverified}; at escalated (a :review_missing hold taken in the landing's transaction, or any other) it moves nothing, the hold event alone holding the item. When no independent path is touched, or the fact is :ok, it writes nothing.

An independent_hold is open until independent_verification/2 is :ok for its landed revision. While one is open: a holder resolution (US-52.31) of the item is refused 409 independent_verification, changing nothing, whatever reason moved it into escalated (:review_missing included); and every path that reaches verified (verify, verify-all, bulk verify, backfill and bulk mark-complete, beside ReviewCustody.ensure_landed_review/3) is refused 409 independent_verification unless the verify is the independent one itself: a verify by a dispatch that passes US-52.12's separation and host checks against the implementer at the landed revision is accepted, because it is the act that makes independent_verification/2 :ok. Each of those paths is also refused while the item's ChgIndependentPathsWorker job for its landed revision has not completed, so no independent landing reaches verified before it is judged. A human resolution is unaffected.

The independent verify that AC-52.31a.3 accepts, once it commits and independent_verification/2 is :ok for an open hold's landed revision, closes the hold and, in the same transaction, returns an item that entered escalated over :independent_unverified to the stage it left (merged or deployed) over the new control-only edge {:escalated, from, :independent_verified}, carrying the identities that stage requires (merge_sha at merged, stage_machine.ex:628), so the landed change continues toward deployed and verified and is never re-queued and implemented a second time. An item escalated for another reason (:review_missing) stays escalated and leaves as that reason allows.

The 409 independent_verification refusal is documented where callers read it: the resolve endpoint's operation/2 OpenAPI spec and those of the verify routes list it, the MCP resolve_escalation and verify_story descriptions name it and say that a separated verifier's recorded verification of the landed revision clears it, and CHANGELOG.md records the new 409 as an API change.

technical_notes: chg route: the landed effect is EventEffects.after_move/5 for 'landed' (lib/loopctl/changes/event_effects.ex:564), where the :review_missing hold is taken through escalate_raw/5. The landed diff is a forge read (PullRequestSource.compare/3, pull_request_source.ex:384), so it is never made inside the event transaction: the landed effect enqueues the job in that transaction, and the job reads the diff, runs Gate B with the repo's independent_paths, and escalates under the story lock when the fact is not :ok.

Stage machine: {:merged, :escalated, :independent_unverified}, {:deployed, :escalated, :independent_unverified}, {:escalated, :merged, :independent_verified} and {:escalated, :deployed, :independent_verified} join @transitions (lib/loopctl/delivery/stage_machine.ex:286) beside the @release_escalations-style control-only reasons, and Stages.advance/4 refuses them from any caller but the job and the verification record (the @release_only_edges pattern, stages.ex:2114). Every edge out of escalated is chained (chained?/3, :865). The return edges go back to the stage the item left, never to queued, because the change has already landed: re-queueing it would implement and land it a second time (stage_machine.ex:170-171).

Which sha: the landed revision is event.sha, the revision commit, and never data.merge_sha (CLAUDE.md, chg-dispatched reviews; event_effects.ex:552-565). Verification records and the job's uniqueness key on it; merge_sha is used only to read what landed on trunk.

Hold: the resolve refusal runs in Escalations.resolve/3's pre-release block (US-52.31) beside the review_missing check (AC-52.31.5), so a refused resolve destroys nothing (the #862 rule); the verify refusal runs beside ReviewCustody.ensure_landed_review/3 on every path CLAUDE.md lists for it. The open-hold read is one function both call.

Documentation (CLAUDE.md, an API constraint goes in the endpoint's operation/2 spec; an operator-facing refusal is named in its MCP tool's description): the resolve operation is in lib/loopctl_web/controllers/story_escalation_controller.ex, the verify operations in story_verification_controller.ex; the tool descriptions in mcp-server/index.js, pinned by a node --test case.
independent_verification/2 and Gate B's :independent outcome are provided by US-52.12; the holder resolve edge and its pre-release block by US-52.31.
non_goals: A chg-side check before chg lands: loopctl judges the landing it is told about (US-52.12 non-goals).
Changing how a pull-request merge is gated: US-52.12.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.31a.2: the job is enqueued in the landed event's own transaction, so a landing that commits always carries its check; a lost connection to the forge fails one attempt, which Oban retries, and only the last attempt's failure holds the item.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.31a.1: the check is an Oban job row in loopctl's Postgres and the hold is a stage event; a restart or deploy loses neither, and AC-52.31a.3 keeps the item from verified until the job has run.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.31a.1: the job is unique per story and landed revision, so a redelivered landed event or a retried job holds at most once.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.31a.2: the forge read runs in the job, outside chg's event apply, so a slow forge never holds a landing; a diff still unreadable on the last attempt holds the item rather than passing it.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.31a.1: the job runs on any loopctl node through Oban and reaches the item by its story id.

definition_of_done: On production, a chg-landed change touching an independent path with no separated verifier shows an :independent_unverified escalation on its timeline, a holder's resolve is refused until the verification is recorded, and the recorded verification returns it to merged over :independent_verified.
defaults: A landed diff still unreadable after the job's 5 attempts holds the item (fail closed).
A verified independent landing returns to the stage it left (merged or deployed), not to queued.
